# LynxDB

> Query log files from the shell or keep logs on a server with a Web UI. One binary for Linux, macOS and Windows, with PPL in both modes.

Every page of this site is also Markdown: at its address with `.md` in place of the closing slash (`/blog/slug/` at `/blog/slug.md`, `/blog/` at `/blog.md`, the home page at `/index.md`), or at the page's own address when the request sends `Accept: text/markdown`. The links below go to the Markdown.

## Website

- [LynxDB: a log database you can pipe into](https://lynxdb.org/index.md): Query log files from the shell or keep logs on a server with a Web UI. One binary for Linux, macOS and Windows, with PPL in both modes.
- [LynxDB blog](https://lynxdb.org/blog.md): Querying logs with LynxDB, how its engine reads them, and what each release changes.

## Documentation and source

- [Documentation](https://docs.lynxdb.org/): LynxDB reference and guides.
- [Quick start](https://docs.lynxdb.org/docs/getting-started/quickstart/): Run a local query or start a server.
- [PPL reference](https://docs.lynxdb.org/docs/ppl/overview/): Piped Processing Language syntax and examples.
- [Source code](https://github.com/lynxbase/lynxdb): LynxDB source and release history.

## Blog posts

- [Five questions for an access log, answered from the shell](https://lynxdb.org/blog/querying-an-access-log.md): lynxdb query loads a log file, runs one PPL query over it and exits, with no server to start. We ask a 1,000-line access log where its server errors come from and when they happened.
- [Fourteen blocks of 61,246: how LynxDB answers JSONBench in 0.18 s](https://lynxdb.org/blog/lynxdb-on-jsonbench.md): LynxDB answers JSONBench's five queries over 1 billion Bluesky events in 0.18 s on a warm cache; ClickHouse's published result is 6.9 s. Most of the answer comes from metadata kept per block: the exact distinct count in Q2 opens 14 of 61,246 blocks. Without its sort key LynxDB takes 10.2 s, and ClickHouse is faster.
- [Twenty-eight bytes from the end: inside the LynxDB engine](https://lynxdb.org/blog/inside-the-lynxdb-engine.md): LynxDB opens a part file from its last 28 bytes, which locate a footer that describes every block: its first sort key, its key runs, its rows per hour. This post follows the Bluesky events from JSON lines into that footer, shows which queries end there and what the design costs, and sets each piece beside ClickHouse's MergeTree.
